summary: Plan a3-note-rename-001 passed expand and backfill stages, adding and populating customer_note. However deploy_new_001.django_migrate failed with ProgrammingError: column customer_note already exists, because the column persisted from prior aborted migration attempts (a1/a2). The expand stage re-added the column, and the new-app migration lacked an existence check, causing a duplicate column error. Both note and customer_note columns remained, violating the single-column rename intent.
revision_notes: Root cause: Residual customer_note column from earlier aborted plans (a1/a2) was not dropped or checked for existence before plan a3's expand stage re-added it, and the new-app Django migration had no idempotency guard, causing the duplicate column error.

stages.description: Add new column customer_note alongside existing note column to allow both app versions to operate concurrently.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy values from the deprecated note column into customer_note so the new app can read the data.
Deploy the new application version (new-staged) which is already coded to read/write the customer_note column. No code changes are required from this plan; the deployment is performed separately.
Retire the old application version (old) that still references the note column. After this stage only the new version runs, which exclusively uses customer_note.
Remove the old note column after data has been migrated and old app is retired, leaving only customer_note.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
